subject: science
passage: In the 1990s, divers off Amami Oshima, an island in southern Japan, began reporting strange circles in the sand of the seafloor. Each circle was about two meters across, with ridges and grooves running out from its center. Years later, scientists learned who made them: a male pufferfish only about 12 centimeters long. The fish builds each circle by swimming along the bottom and flapping its fins, and females lay their eggs in its center.
stem: According to the text, how does the male pufferfish make a sand circle?

choices.A: By swimming along the seafloor while flapping its fins
choices.B: By pushing sand into ridges with its mouth
choices.C: By working together with several female pufferfish
choices.D: By following grooves left in the sand by ocean currents

explanation.why: The question asks how the circle is made. The last sentence answers it directly: "The fish builds each circle by swimming along the bottom and flapping its fins." The correct choice restates this.
explanation.A: Correct. The text says the fish "builds each circle by swimming along the bottom and flapping its fins."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the fish uses its mouth to move sand.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the male builds the circle; females only lay their eggs in its center.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the fish makes the ridges and grooves; it never mentions ocean currents.
